subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Normal vesicular breath sounds are heard:

options.A: Over most of the lung fields, with inspiration longer than expiration

questions.explanation: Bronchial breathing (equal inspiration and expiration with a pause) over the peripheral lung indicates consolidation.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A high-pitched continuous musical sound heard mainly during expiration is a:
questions.explanation: Wheeze indicates narrowed airways as in asthma and COPD; stridor is an inspiratory sound from upper airway obstruction.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Fine late-inspiratory crackles at both lung bases are characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Coarse crackles that change with coughing suggest secretions (bronchiectasis, pneumonia).
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Stridor is a sign of:
questions.explanation: Medical emergency; causes include foreign body, croup, laryngeal oedema.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Cheyne–Stokes respiration is a pattern of:

options.B: Cyclical waxing and waning of breath depth alternating with apnoea

questions.explanation: Seen in heart failure, raised intracranial pressure and at the end of life; Kussmaul breathing is deep and rapid in metabolic acidosis.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Deep, rapid (air hunger) Kussmaul breathing is typical of:
questions.explanation: A compensatory respiratory response to metabolic acidosis.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In a large right-sided pleural effusion the trachea is:

options.D: Shifted to the LEFT, away from the effusion

questions.explanation: Collapse/fibrosis pulls the trachea toward the lesion; effusion and tension pneumothorax push it away.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Paradoxical (see-saw) abdominal movement during inspiration suggests:

options.D: Diaphragmatic paralysis or severe respiratory muscle fatigue

questions.explanation: The abdomen moves inward on inspiration when the diaphragm fails; commonly seen in tetraplegia and GBS.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The MRC dyspnoea scale grades:

options.A: Breathlessness related to activities of daily living

questions.explanation: Grades 1–5, from breathless only on strenuous exercise to too breathless to leave the house.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The six-minute walk test is used to assess:
questions.explanation: Distance walked in 6 minutes along a 30-m corridor; used in COPD, heart failure and pulmonary hypertension.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A peak expiratory flow meter is mainly used to monitor:
questions.explanation: Diurnal variation >20% suggests asthma.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: FEV1 is the volume of air:

options.B: Forcibly exhaled in the first second after a maximal inspiration
options.C: Remaining in the lung after expiration

questions.explanation: FEV1/FVC below 0.7 indicates airflow obstruction.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: On a chest X-ray, a pneumothorax appears as:

options.A: A white opacity with an air bronchogram
options.C: A visible pleural line with absent lung markings beyond it

questions.explanation: A meniscus sign suggests pleural effusion; air bronchograms suggest consolidation.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Central cyanosis is best observed on the:
questions.explanation: Peripheral cyanosis affects the extremities due to poor perfusion.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Positive expiratory pressure (PEP) therapy helps clear secretions by:

options.B: Splinting small airways open during expiration and allowing collateral ventilation

questions.explanation: Used in cystic fibrosis, bronchiectasis and COPD; flutter and acapella valves add oscillation.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The oscillating PEP (flutter) device combines:

options.D: Positive expiratory pressure with airway vibrations

questions.explanation: Oscillations reduce sputum viscosity and loosen secretions.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Autogenic drainage is a technique in which the patient:

options.C: Uses controlled breathing at different lung volumes to mobilise secretions from small to large airways

questions.explanation: Breathing at low lung volume to unstick, medium to collect and high to evacuate.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Humidification of inspired oxygen helps by:

options.B: Reducing the viscosity of secretions and preventing mucosal drying

questions.explanation: Essential for patients on high-flow oxygen or with artificial airways.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Nebulised bronchodilators should ideally be given:

options.A: Before chest physiotherapy to improve airway clearance

questions.explanation: Timing optimises secretion clearance.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A mechanical insufflation–exsufflation device (cough assist) is mainly used for patients with:
questions.explanation: Applies positive then negative pressure to simulate a cough.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Manual hyperinflation (bagging) in ventilated patients is used to:

options.A: Re-expand collapsed lung and mobilise secretions

questions.explanation: A slow deep inspiration, an inspiratory pause and a fast release increase expiratory flow.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Suction through an endotracheal tube should be applied:

options.D: Only while withdrawing the catheter, for no more than 10–15 seconds

questions.explanation: Hypoxia, mucosal trauma and arrhythmias are risks.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) is most useful in:

options.D: Acute cardiogenic pulmonary oedema and obstructive sleep apnoea

questions.explanation: Maintains alveolar recruitment and reduces work of breathing.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Bilevel positive airway pressure (BiPAP) differs from CPAP in providing:

options.C: Higher inspiratory pressure than expiratory pressure to assist ventilation

questions.explanation: Used for acute hypercapnic respiratory failure in COPD exacerbation.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In which ventilator mode does the patient trigger each breath and receive support with pressure during inspiration?
questions.explanation: PSV is used for weaning.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A good predictor that a ventilated patient can be weaned successfully is:

options.A: Spontaneous breathing trial with adequate tidal volume and low rapid-shallow-breathing index

questions.explanation: RSBI (f/Vt) below 105 predicts success.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Critical illness polyneuropathy/myopathy is best minimised by:

options.A: Early mobilisation and minimising sedation and immobility

questions.explanation: Early rehabilitation reduces ICU-acquired weakness and shortens ventilation time.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which finding would usually contraindicate mobilising an ICU patient?

options.A: Unstable arrhythmias, active myocardial ischaemia or MAP < 60 mmHg

questions.explanation: Safety criteria include haemodynamic stability and acceptable oxygenation.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Prone positioning in ARDS improves oxygenation mainly by:

options.C: Improving ventilation–perfusion matching by recruiting dorsal lung regions

questions.explanation: The effect is maximal when applied for >12 h/day in severe ARDS.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Pulse oximetry may give a falsely high reading in:
questions.explanation: Carboxyhaemoglobin is read as oxyhaemoglobin.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A resting heart rate below 60 beats per minute is termed:
questions.explanation: Athletes may have physiological bradycardia.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A ‘saw-tooth’ pattern of atrial activity on an ECG indicates:
questions.explanation: Atrial rate ~300/min with variable AV block.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In a patient with a permanent pacemaker, exercise precaution includes:

options.C: Avoiding heavy upper-limb resistance and sudden vigorous movement over the device site in the early weeks

questions.explanation: Shortwave diathermy and electrical stimulation near the pacemaker are contraindicated.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The Karvonen formula calculates target heart rate using:

options.C: Heart rate reserve (HRmax − HRrest) multiplied by intensity plus resting HR

questions.explanation: e.g. 60–80% heart rate reserve plus resting HR.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The Bruce protocol is a standardised:
questions.explanation: Speed and incline increase every 3 minutes.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: An absolute contraindication to exercise testing is:

options.C: Acute myocardial infarction within 2 days or unstable angina

questions.explanation: Also acute pulmonary embolism, severe symptomatic aortic stenosis and uncontrolled arrhythmias.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A normal blood pressure response to progressive dynamic exercise is:

options.A: A gradual rise in systolic pressure with little change in diastolic
options.C: A rise in diastolic over 100 mmHg

questions.explanation: A fall in systolic BP with increasing workload signals poor left ventricular function.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: After open-heart surgery, early physiotherapy mainly aims to:

options.A: Keep the patient in bed for 2 weeks
options.C: Prevent respiratory complications and restore early mobility within sternal precautions

questions.explanation: Includes breathing exercises, supported coughing, ankle exercises and early walking.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Following cardiac transplantation, the heart rate response to exercise is:

options.D: Delayed and blunted because of denervation

questions.explanation: The donor heart has no vagal or sympathetic innervation; it relies on circulating catecholamines, so longer warm-up and cool-down are needed.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Pitting oedema that rebounds within 2–3 seconds with a depth of about 4 mm is graded as:
questions.explanation: 1+ 2 mm; 2+ 4 mm; 3+ 6 mm; 4+ 8 mm with prolonged rebound.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The maximal heart rate in older adults is generally:
questions.explanation: Maximal HR falls with age by about one beat per year.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: After thoracotomy the physiotherapist should particularly teach:

options.A: Shoulder range-of-motion exercises on the operated side, deep breathing and supported coughing

questions.explanation: Prevents frozen shoulder and respiratory complications.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The best position to optimise lung volumes after abdominal surgery is:
questions.explanation: Upright positioning increases functional residual capacity.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Early post-operative mobilisation helps to prevent:

options.B: Chest infection, DVT and pressure sores

questions.explanation: Also reduces length of stay.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Anti-embolism stockings are used to:

options.C: Reduce the risk of deep vein thrombosis by improving venous return

questions.explanation: Contraindicated in severe peripheral arterial disease.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Effective analgesia before post-operative chest physiotherapy:

options.A: Improves ability to breathe deeply and cough

questions.explanation: Pain limits lung expansion and cough, promoting atelectasis.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A patient with a colostomy should avoid:

options.C: Heavy straining and lifting that raises intra-abdominal pressure (risk of parastomal hernia)

questions.explanation: Educate on stoma care and core stability exercises when cleared.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: After a transtibial amputation, pillows under the knee should be avoided because they encourage:
questions.explanation: Also avoid prolonged sitting with the knee flexed.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Phantom limb pain after amputation is best managed initially by:
questions.explanation: Medication may be needed.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The commonest cause of foot ulceration in diabetes is:
questions.explanation: Daily foot inspection, proper footwear and avoidance of barefoot walking are vital.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Arterial ulcers are typically:

options.A: Painful, punched-out, over the toes or pressure points with absent pulses
options.C: Painless and over the medial malleolus

questions.explanation: Compression is contraindicated until ABPI is checked.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The ankle–brachial pressure index (ABPI) below which compression bandaging is contraindicated is about:
questions.explanation: Normal ABPI is 1.0–1.3; <0.9 indicates peripheral arterial disease.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Negative pressure wound therapy works by:

options.D: Applying controlled suction that removes exudate and promotes granulation

questions.explanation: Contraindicated over exposed vessels and untreated osteomyelitis.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The Braden scale predicts the risk of:
questions.explanation: Scores subcategories: sensory perception, moisture, activity, mobility, nutrition, friction/shear.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Pressure garment therapy for burn scars is applied to:

options.B: Reduce hypertrophic scarring by applying constant pressure (about 24–30 mmHg)

questions.explanation: Worn for 23 hours a day for up to 12–18 months.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The initial priority of physiotherapy in an acute burn patient is:

options.A: Correct positioning and splinting to prevent contractures

questions.explanation: Plus chest care if inhalation injury is present.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In cancer-related fatigue the best evidence-based physiotherapy intervention is:

options.A: Individualised graded aerobic and resistance exercise

questions.explanation: Exercise is safe and beneficial during and after treatment.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In a patient with bone metastases, exercise should avoid:

options.B: Upper-limb exercise away from the lesion
options.C: High-impact loading and heavy resistance through the affected bone

questions.explanation: Pathological fracture risk; use Mirels' score for risk assessment.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A person at risk of lymphoedema should be advised to:

options.D: Avoid blood pressure measurement, injections and heat on the at-risk limb and maintain skin care

questions.explanation: Gentle progressive exercise is safe.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Sarcopenia is defined as:

options.C: Age-related loss of skeletal muscle mass and strength

questions.explanation: Resistance training and protein intake are effective.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which is a component of Fried's frailty phenotype?

options.D: Unintentional weight loss, exhaustion, low physical activity, slow gait and weak grip

questions.explanation: Three or more criteria define frailty.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which test best predicts fall risk in older adults?

options.C: Timed Up and Go or Berg Balance Scale

questions.explanation: A history of falls, polypharmacy and gait impairment increase risk.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: An absolute contraindication to aerobic exercise in pregnancy is:

options.A: Severe pre-eclampsia, persistent second/third trimester bleeding or placenta praevia after 26 weeks

questions.explanation: Also pre-term labour and ruptured membranes.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In a healthy pregnant woman, appropriate exercise intensity can be monitored by:

options.B: The talk test and a rating of perceived exertion of about 12–14

questions.explanation: Avoid exercise in heat and activities with a risk of falling.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Pelvic girdle pain in pregnancy is commonly managed with:

options.A: Pelvic support belts, activity modification and stabilising exercises

questions.explanation: Avoid asymmetrical postures and wide leg abduction.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In children with cystic fibrosis, airway clearance should be performed:

options.A: Daily, with age-appropriate techniques, before meals or two hours after

questions.explanation: Regular exercise also supports airway clearance.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A physiotherapist treating a child with Down syndrome should be cautious about:

options.D: Atlantoaxial instability when performing neck movements and sports

questions.explanation: Screen before activities such as gymnastics or trampolining.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which statement about physiotherapy for HIV-positive patients is correct?

options.B: Exercise is beneficial and standard precautions are sufficient
options.D: Masks must be worn by the patient

questions.explanation: Exercise improves strength and quality of life.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: For weight loss in obese individuals, the exercise recommendation is:

options.A: Gradually build up to 150–300 minutes a week of moderate aerobic activity plus resistance training
options.D: High-intensity impact exercise from the start

questions.explanation: Non-weight-bearing options such as swimming and cycling reduce joint load.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which is NOT a component of the metabolic syndrome?
questions.explanation: Also reduced HDL and hypertension.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The most effective intervention to slow lung function decline in COPD is:
questions.explanation: Physiotherapists can deliver brief advice.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Pulmonary rehabilitation in COPD includes:
questions.explanation: Typically 6–8 weeks of twice-weekly supervised sessions; improves dyspnoea and quality of life.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Long-term oxygen therapy in COPD is indicated when the resting PaO₂ is below:
questions.explanation: Used for at least 15 hours per day to improve survival.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)
